summary: A fast shove into frame that overshoots and rings out. An impact, a slam, a title landing.
doc:
Use for the moment something ARRIVES: a hard stop, a door slamming, a card hitting the screen, a joke landing.

The hit is a step and everything after it is one damped spring, so the recovery can never look unrelated to the blow - which is the usual tell of a hand-keyframed shake. Position and roll are driven off the same oscillator as the zoom, so the whole frame moves as one object.

Keep `overshoot` small. Past about 0.08 it stops reading as an impact and starts reading as a zoom effect.

win_w.doc: window width in plate px at zoom 1.

win_h.doc: window height in plate px at zoom 1.

t_hit.doc: seconds of rush before the impact.

overshoot.doc: how far past z_rest the hit throws it. Small.

freq.doc: ring frequency, Hz. Higher = tighter, more rigid.

shake.doc: px of positional throw riding the same oscillator.

roll.doc: degrees of roll riding the same oscillator.

brake_slam.note: A vehicle stopping dead, seen head on.

title_card.note: Tighter and more rigid - for a card or a logo landing.
